about.diet: Adults eat mostly mid-water prey: mullets, pinfish, marine catfishes; crabs are a spring favorite at inlets
about.depth: Normal habitat to about 30 m; tolerates salinities from fresh to about 47 ppt
about.behavior: Migratory and heat-loving. Adults arrive in the Florida Keys in April once surface water reaches about 26 C, peak in May (26-28 C) and leave in June (27-29 C). Cold fronts push them to warmer, deeper water, and juveniles leave creeks below about 20 C.
about.spawning: April to June in the Florida Keys
about.regulations_note: Florida prohibits the commercial sale of tarpon. Check FWC rules before keeping any tarpon.
about.timing_note: Angler lore: patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies. Numbers are judgment calls to be calibrated against trip logs.

reasons.text: Water is 26.9 C, inside the 25-29 C range where tarpon run.
The tide is falling (Virginia Key); moving water through passes is when tarpon feed.
This is an inlet or pass. Tarpon travel through passes and feed on crabs and baitfish the tide carries.
It is night, a favored time for tarpon around passes and bridges.
It is outside the spring and early-summer tarpon run, so far fewer tarpon are in South Florida passes.
